record.title: THE OBJECT AND AFFECTS OF ENVY AND EMULATION.
record.subjects: Envy ; Imitative behavior ; Philosophy of religion ; Belief & doubt ; Virtues ; Vices ; Religion ; Aristotle, 384-322 B.C.
record.abstract: An essay is presented on the relevance of envy and emulation in the philosophy of religion. It examines virtues to determine the impact of right and wrong perceptions on belief and practice. The subjective dimensions of envy and emulation are explored based on philosopher Aristotle's views on both emotions. Other topics include analytic and continental philosophy, the gap between virtue and vice and the differences between envy and emulation.

record.title: DISPOSITIONS, HABITS AND VIRTUES: COMMENTS ON MULDER AND KELLY.
record.subjects: Disposition (Philosophy) ; Habit ; Virtues ; Envy ; Imitative behavior ; Kierkegaard, Søren, 1813-1855 ; Aristotle, 384-322 B.C.
record.abstract: The article presents the author's views on dispositions, habits and virtues, highlighting the essays by Jack Mulder on philosopher Soren Kierkegaard's heritage on continental philosophy and Michael Kelly on the differences between emulation and envy. Also discussed are philosopher Aristotle's beliefs on habit and virtue, Mulder's claim that love is not a static property, and Kierkegaard's argument that love is unconditional.

record.title: GOD AND ARGUMENT.
record.subjects: Proof of God ; Debate ; Atheism ; Philosophy of religion ; Moser, Paul
record.abstract: The article presents the author's views on debates on God's existence as of 2015 with regard to why they have persisted and have not been concluded, highlighting philosopher Paul Moser's opinion on the issue. He states that there have been numerous debates on God's existence which is the most significant philosophical issue. Two cynical theories on the issue are explored as well as the arguments of theists and atheists. Other topics include the argument that God is worthy of worship.

record.title: GOD AND EPISTEMIC AUTHORITY.
record.subjects: God in Christianity ; Virtue epistemology ; Epistemic logic ; Personality ; Idolatry
record.abstract: The article presents the author's views on God and epistemic authority. He explores human beings' fabrication of gods for various reasons which include to reflect their imperfect traits. God's epistemic authority is discussed as well as how it can benefit an epistemiology of people's understanding of God. Other topics include epistemic idolatry, curative knowledge, and God's characterstics.

record.title: THE WEIRD PLACE OF GOD DEBATES IN THE ACADEMIC STUDY OF RELIGIONS.
record.subjects: Proof of God ; Philosophy of religion ; Philosophy & religion ; Aikin, Scott F. ; Moser, Paul K.
record.abstract: The article presents the author's views on the debates about God's existence in the academic study of religions, highlighting the possible mash-ups between the philosophy of religion and other disciplines. He critiques the articles by Scott F. Aikin and Paul K. Moser on the philosophy of religion which are published within the issue. Also discussed are the advantages and disadvantages of mash-ups.
